column1: In an SSDT unit test, use the {{c1::pre-test}} script to prepare the data needed by the test.
column2:
The pre-test script establishes the starting state for the main test. For example, insert an order that the test can update. Set up only the data the test needs.
Review source

column1: In an SSDT unit test, use the {{c1::post-test}} script to clean up data after the test action.
column2:
The post-test script can delete or reset rows that the main action changed. Without cleanup, a later test can pass or fail because of data a previous test left behind.
Review source

column1: The SSDT {{c1::Data Checksum}} condition compares a result set with an expected checksum.
column2:
A checksum summarizes the returned data for comparison with a known result. Changing values such as timestamps or generated IDs can alter that summary even when the tested behavior has not changed.
Review source

column1: Use the SSDT {{c1::Empty ResultSet}} condition to require that a query returns no rows.
column2:
This condition passes only when the query returns zero rows. For example, search for orphaned records and expect no matches. It does not mean each returned cell is blank.
Review source

column1: The SSDT {{c1::Execution Time}} condition fails a test when its main T-SQL script exceeds the configured time limit.
column2:
The limit applies to the main test script. Setup and cleanup can add to the overall reported duration without using up this condition's limit. Use a stable test environment for timing checks.
Review source

column1: Mark an SSDT test method that expects a SQL error with the {{c1::ExpectedSqlException}} attribute.
column2:
This attribute marks the expected SQL exception. Specify MessageNumber when the exact error identifies the rule under test. An unexpected SQL error must not count as evidence that the rule worked.
Review source

column1: In ExpectedSqlException, {{c1::MatchFirstError=false}} searches every SqlError in the exception for a match.
column2:
One SQL exception can contain several errors. With MatchFirstError=false the attribute searches the full error list. The default only checks the first, which can miss an expected error reported later.
Review source

column1: SSDT stores a test project's database connections and deployment configuration in {{c1::app.config}}.
column2:
The configuration file tells the test runner where to connect and what to deploy. Supply CI credentials through protected configuration rather than committing a working password in the file.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server Object Explorer, generate an SSDT test stub for a procedure with {{c1::Create Unit Tests}}.
column2:
The generated stub is a starting point for the chosen database object. Add inputs and expected results, then remove the placeholder condition. Generating the stub does not establish that the procedure works.
Review source

column1: For assembly-based test selection, VSTest@3 takes test DLL patterns in its {{c1::testAssemblyVer2}} input.
column2:
testAssemblyVer2 supplies patterns for compiled test assemblies. The patterns are evaluated within the configured search folder. This option selects DLLs, not SQL project source files.
Review source

column1: For an SDK-style test project using VSTest, run {{c1::dotnet test DatabaseTests.csproj}} from its directory.
column2:
Run dotnet test against the test project that contains the test framework and compatible adapter. The test project drives the checks. The SQL project builds the database schema package instead.
Review source
